items.title: Expectation-maximization
items.statement: For a jointly measurable normalized complete-data density and fixed observed data on a positive finite marginal fiber, form the current latent conditional density and maximize the expected complete-data log density; an optional generalized update accepts any admissible candidate whose Q value does not decrease. The procedure makes no convergence claim.

references.title: A. P. Dempster, N. M. Laird and D. B. Rubin, Maximum likelihood from incomplete data via the EM algorithm
Mario A. T. Figueiredo, Lecture Notes on the EM Algorithm (2004)

items.title: EM does not decrease the observed log likelihood
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. On a positive finite observed-data fiber, when the current and candidate complete-data log densities are integrable under the current latent conditional law, the candidate latent law dominates the current one, and their directional KL divergence is finite, the observed log-likelihood difference equals the Q difference plus that KL divergence. Hence any exact or generalized M-step with nondecreasing Q does not decrease the observed log likelihood.

references.title: A. P. Dempster, N. M. Laird and D. B. Rubin, Maximum likelihood from incomplete data via the EM algorithm
Mario A. T. Figueiredo, Lecture Notes on the EM Algorithm (2004)

items.title: Generalized EM does not decrease the observed log likelihood under Q-ascent
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of the observed-likelihood identity, every admissible candidate with Q(theta|theta_t) at least Q(theta_t|theta_t) has observed log likelihood at least that of theta_t; the Q maximizer need not be attained.

references.title: A. P. Dempster, N. M. Laird and D. B. Rubin, Maximum likelihood from incomplete data via the EM algorithm
Mario A. T. Figueiredo, Lecture Notes on the EM Algorithm (2004)

items.title: Likelihood ascent alone gives no global optimality or convergence conclusion
items.statement: The EM ascent results are one-step, fixed-data inequalities. They do not establish boundedness of the likelihood sequence, convergence of parameter iterates, stationarity of limit points, or global optimality. Multiple maximizing updates and covariance-collapse examples exhibit limits of the ascent conclusion.

references.title: A. P. Dempster, N. M. Laird and D. B. Rubin, Maximum likelihood from incomplete data via the EM algorithm
Mario A. T. Figueiredo, Lecture Notes on the EM Algorithm (2004)

title: Latent-variable EM and likelihood ascent — Examples

items.title: Responsibilities in a two-component mixture
items.statement: For a two-component mixture with weights (1/3, 2/3) and component densities taking values (2, 1) at the observation, the observed density is 4/3 and the latent-label conditional probabilities are (1/2, 1/2). The corresponding Q function is the responsibility-weighted complete-data log density.

references.title: A. P. Dempster, N. M. Laird and D. B. Rubin, Maximum likelihood from incomplete data via the EM algorithm
Steffen L. Lauritzen, The EM algorithm for Bayesian networks (Lecture 8, 2003)

items.title: A generalized EM step can increase Q without maximizing it
items.statement: In a two-Bernoulli complete-data model at current parameter 1/2, the candidate 7/10 strictly raises Q and the observed log likelihood, while the exact Q maximizer is 3/4.

references.title: A. P. Dempster, N. M. Laird and D. B. Rubin, Maximum likelihood from incomplete data via the EM algorithm
Mario A. T. Figueiredo, Lecture Notes on the EM Algorithm (2004)

items.title: An EM likelihood with two strict local maxima
items.statement: A valid latent model on parameter space [-2, 2] has two strict local maxima of the observed likelihood at -1 and 1, both tied global maximizers; because both also maximize Q, an exact M-step selection can alternate between them and the parameter iterates need not converge.

references.title: A. P. Dempster, N. M. Laird and D. B. Rubin, Maximum likelihood from incomplete data via the EM algorithm
Mario A. T. Figueiredo, Lecture Notes on the EM Algorithm (2004)

items.title: Gaussian mixture likelihood is unbounded under covariance collapse
items.statement: For observations 0 and 1 under a two-component univariate Gaussian mixture with unknown component variance, fixing one component at N(0, epsilon squared) and the other at N(1, 1) makes the likelihood tend to infinity as epsilon decreases to zero.

references.title: A. P. Dempster, N. M. Laird and D. B. Rubin, Maximum likelihood from incomplete data via the EM algorithm
Mario A. T. Figueiredo, Lecture Notes on the EM Algorithm (2004)

items.title: A support-losing candidate has infinite directional KL
items.statement: With a binary latent variable and constant observed marginal, the move from current latent law (1/2, 1/2) to candidate law (1, 0) loses support, has infinite KL in the current-to-candidate direction, and gives Q equal to negative infinity.

references.title: A. P. Dempster, N. M. Laird and D. B. Rubin, Maximum likelihood from incomplete data via the EM algorithm
Mario A. T. Figueiredo, Lecture Notes on the EM Algorithm (2004)
